# OpenKB - Creating your smart knowledge base

OpenKB is an open source tool that transforms documents into a local wiki, connected and maintained by AI, without vector database. Video shows configuration, queries, PageIndex tree structure, watch mode, Obsidian view, AGENTS.md file, and base check command.

Video by Maurício Yokoyama Issei, published on May 7, 2026 (5 min 59 s).
Watch: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hdFXMDVb7Og

_The video and the transcript are in Portuguese. The minutes between brackets, such as [04:12], point to the excerpt of the video._

## A knowledge base without vectors

OpenKB is an open source tool for building a local knowledge base without using vectors [00:00]. It takes raw documents and compiles them into a structured, connected and managed wiki by AI [00:00].

## Initial Settings

To begin with, turn `openkb init` on the terminal, choose the model in LiteLLM format, such as Anthropic's Claude Sonnet, and put the API key in the `.env` file [00:43].

OpenKB already comes with Gateway LiteLLM, which links providers like OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini [01:05]. According to the video, this gives access to more than 100 models, and you can switch models without rewriting code [01:27].

## PageIndex Queries and Structure

For a quick question, use `openkb query`. For an investigation in several rounds, use `openkb chat`, which saves the session history [01:48].

The traditional RAG breaks the documents into thousands of pieces of vector and, with each question, tries to rediscover everything from scratch [02:09]. OpenKB, with PageIndex, compiles information in a hierarchical tree, similar to an index, and knowledge accumulates [02:29].

The PageIndex documentation summarizes: "Similarity is not relevance" [02:29]. In a long PDF, the tool creates index trees with abstracts, and the AI runs through this tree to find the page or section that has the answer [02:50].

## Automation with watch mode

The `openkb watch` command runs in the background and observes the folder `raw` [03:10]. When you release a PDF, Word or text there, the AI reads the file, generates the abstracts and updates the concepts and crossed links [03:31].

## Obsidian View

OpenKB generates Markdown files with double wikilinks [03:31]. When opening the wiki folder in Obsidian, navigation becomes fluid and the graph shows the connection between ideas [03:52].

## The AGENTS.md file

The `AGENTS.md` is the IA instruction manual: defines the standard, conventions and how to organize information [04:13]. The AI reads the file every run. If you change a rule, the base organization changes on time without restarting anything [04:34].

## The health of the base

With more documents, redundancies and duplications arise [04:34]. The `openkb lint` command scans for contradictions, orphaned links, information gaps and old content [04:56].

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Do I need a vector bank?

Nope. OpenKB organizes knowledge in a hierarchical tree without vectors [02:29].

### How to keep the base up to date effortlessly?

Let `openkb watch` run: it processes each new file that falls into the folder `raw` [03:10].

## Fonts

- [OpenKB (Open LLM Knowledge Base)](https://github.com/VectifyAI/OpenKB): OpenKB commands (init, query, chat, watch and lint) and the Markdown wiki generated from the documents.
- [PageIndex (Document Index for Vectorless RAG)](https://github.com/VectifyAI/PageIndex): The tree structure with abstracts, without vectors, and the phrase "similarity is not relevant".
- [LiteLLM (AI Gateway & Python SDK)](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm): LiteLLM connects several AI providers, such as OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini, with a single interface.

## About the video

Find out how to build and manage your own permanent digital brain with OpenKB! In this video, we demonstrate step by step to boot and configure your knowledge base locally
. Understand how the system processes long documents using PageIndex tree hierarchical structure, which allows reasoning-based data recovery without the need for vector databases
.
Also learn how to automate the compilation of new files with watch mode
, integrating LiteLLM to use different AI providers (such as Anthropic or Gemini) in a simplified and unified way
, and configuring Obsidian to natively view wikilinks and graph of your knowledge base
. Finally, we explain the fundamental role of the instruction file (AGENTS.md) to maintain the base structure and guide the LLM
, in addition to how to debug and keep concepts always up to date and without redundancy through integrity checks (lint)
.
